questions.q: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function. If the domain of the function $f(x) = \cos^{-1} \left( \frac{4x + 2[x]}{3} \right)$ is $[\alpha, \beta]$, then $12(\alpha + \beta)$ is equal to:
questions.explain:
The domain of $\cos^{-1}(y)$ is $-1 \le y \le 1$.
So, $-1 \le \frac{4x + 2[x]}{3} \le 1 \implies -3 \le 4x + 2[x] \le 3$.
Let $x = I + f$, where $I = [x]$ and $f = \{x\}$ is the fractional part, so $0 \le f < 1$.
Then, $4x + 2[x] = 4(I + f) + 2I = 6I + 4f$.
Therefore, $-3 \le 6I + 4f \le 3$.
For $I = 0$: $-3 \le 4f \le 3 \implies 0 \le f \le \frac{3}{4}$. So $x \in \left[0, \frac{3}{4}\right]$.
For $I = -1$: $-3 \le -6 + 4f \le 3 \implies 3 \le 4f \le 9 \implies \frac{3}{4} \le f < 1$. So $x \in \left[-\frac{1}{4}, 0\right)$.
For any other integer $I$, no such $f \in [0, 1)$ satisfies the inequality.
Taking the union gives the domain $x \in \left[-\frac{1}{4}, \frac{3}{4}\right]$.
Thus, $\alpha = -\frac{1}{4}$ and $\beta = \frac{3}{4}$.
$12(\alpha + \beta) = 12 \left( -\frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{4} \right) = 12 \left( \frac{1}{2} \right) = 6$.
questions.subject: Mathematics
